correctness.rationale: A complete local center/leaf case split proves the 9-state transfer. The maximum count of (0,1) columns follows from excluding three consecutive ones. Exhaustive equality classifications use cyclic gap-deficits 3k-n=0,1,2 and force the only exceptional (0,2) center-zero columns when n=1 mod 3, with a correct distinguished-position count. Independent full-graph direct enumeration for n=3..6 and separate minimum-type enumeration for n=3..9 corroborate the proof; transfer coefficients were checked through n=16.

value.rationale: A recent paper explicitly highlights extension of Italian-domination polynomial enumeration from trees and cycles to cactus graphs; sunlets form an infinite unicyclic cactus family with interacting pendant and cycle constraints. This gives the full polynomial and a complete, unexpectedly residue-sensitive optimum count, including a special minimum-column type present only when n=1 mod 3. The known scalar minimum does not determine those counts or configurations, and all weights are reproducibly computable from one nine-state transfer.
